current.title: Round 57 DELIVERED — the engine-bundling round (fifth packaged-app session)
current.detail: The owner's tenth Windows test session: the launcher's app-or-site question worked, the SITE launched and ran perfectly end-to-end (dashboard included) — the first confirmed half-win — but the desktop app still failed to reach agent-core, and the engine's stderr finally named the crash: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, all three startup attempts. Root cause: the staged sidecar's node_modules was a pnpm LINK FARM (189 symlinks on POSIX = 189 junctions on the Windows release runner) that tauri-bundler + NSIS pack/extract does not preserve — the installed engine could not resolve its first bare import and died before its first log line, while every Linux-side check passed. Fixed structurally with zero product-code changes: the staging install now uses --config.node-linker=hoisted (npm-style tree of REAL directories; 301.5 MB → 124.6 MB), a zero-links gate fails the staging on ANY symlink/junction (junctions report as symlinks via lstatSync — one walk, both OSes), and the release workflow BOOTS the real staged engine with the real pinned node.exe on windows-latest (same env + ACUTE_READY handshake as the app) BEFORE pnpm tauri build can pack it — a dead engine can never ship again. Verified: 1071/1071 tests, lint/typecheck clean, staged-boot battery (ACUTE_READY + /health 200 + /api/v1/agents 200), hoisting verified on the exact CI pnpm 11.22.0. The owner's re-test: ACUTE.bat → app-or-site → [1] the desktop app → install 0.57.0 → the console should finally print '✓ agent-core is up — port N'.
